newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegoil import seen subdued up to February.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegoil import seen subdued up to February.

text.p: Pakistan vegoil imports will remain subdued up to February 1997 as domestic cottonseed oil production rises, importers said on Thursday.

They said Pakistan, expecting a bumper cotton crop of more than 10 million 375-lb bales, is likely to import slightly less than one million tonnes of vegoil in fiscal 1996/97 (July-June), down from 1.14 million tonnes imported the previous year.

"We expect the monthly average imports of edible oil to drop to around 60,000 tonnes during September to February, from the average of about 100,000 tonnes recorded (in the same period) last year," dealer Kamran Ahmed Siddiqui of Saulat Enterprise told Reuters.
Cotton picking in Pakistan starts in September and tapers off in February.
Dealers say cottonseed oil supply also peaks during the September to February period.
Siddiqui said September imports of palm oil were at 56,130 tonnes, down about 57 percent from August's 129,661 tonnes.
"There has been a rise of around 40 percent in the pace of cotton arrivals from ginneries during September, compared to the same period last year," he said.
Siddiqui predicted domestic cottonseed oil production to hit 475,000 tonnes this fiscal year, from 375,000 tonnes in 1995/96.

Officials say the government's cotton production target of 10 million bales for the 1996/97 fiscal year is up from 9.95 million last year, despite a recent flare-up of pests in the central Punjab province, the major cotton producer.

Siddiqui said production of rapeseed, canola, mustard and sunflower oils was also rising and was likely to yield more than 200,000 tonnes of the four oils this year, compared to 150,000 tonnes in the previous year.

Arif Qasim, vice president of Pakistan Vanaspati Manufacturers Association, speaking to Reuters from Lahore, said high domestic prices of cooking oil resulting in lower consumption would be another major reason for lower vegoil imports.

"The price of ghee (cooking oil) rising from 33 rupees ($0.89) to 40 rupees per kilo within the past few months has already brought local consumption down," Qasim observed. He added that higher domestic production of cottonseed oil will certainly keep imports at around one million tonnes.
"Imports during October to February will remain subdued and the final import figure may not be over one million tonnes," Qasim said.
